title: Hub world transition!
author: EthelUltima
selftext: My game has a chill set of Time Trial modes where there are no enemies or weapons, you just drive around replicas of famous circuits. So I thought it would be cool to have a hub world where you as you get closer it

comments.author: OwoMeji
comments.body:
I REALLY like the transition.

I would approach it differently. I would start with the fully rendered city at rest. The faster I move/more speed I attain,  I would remove color, building height, vector lines, and so on until just the track and the outline of it were visible at the maximum speed of my bike. Making like a tunnel vision effect. If I stopped or crashed the fully rendered world comes in the same way it dissipates. Slowing down from high speed to corner would have a minimal effect or wouldn’t re-render the city within a certain threshold of speed/time since sometimes you have to slow down for corners/turns. What do you think?

It's meant to be a studio where you can view trophies and times, etc. then when you exit it collapses into the hub world. Part of the story, everything is a simlulation!

comments.author: OwoMeji
comments.body: Exactly that. The goal would be to stay “in the zone”. The city while it is beautiful to see, when you’re racing, you want to stay in the zone as long as possible. Maybe big objects don’t glitch out (ferris wheel, crowd in the stands, starting line, etc)

replies.author: EthelUltima
replies.body:
Fairs! It's a spiritual successor to a 1995 DOS game so I wanted to keep it close but not copy it exactly:   
  
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberbykes:\_Shadow\_Racer\_VR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberbykes:_Shadow_Racer_VR)

comments.author: EthelUltima
comments.body: It's part of my game design that everything made in Claude so it won't be to everyone's taste however the game is a spiritual successor to a 1995 DOS game called Cyberbykes Shadowracer VR, so it sounds similar. The voice was also a major part of that game, that's why it is in it. You can turn it off or switch to a male voice. It only announces things, doesn't narrate story, etc.

comments.author: KobSteel
comments.body: Not a big fan of that ASMR-esque sound design, but everything else is pretty good

replies.author: EthelUltima
replies.body: It's fair, some say it is "too sexy" when I was aiming for sultry.  You can turn it off or switch to male one. It's part of the original 1995 games identity so it's important to have. More voice options is something I will look into later when most of the spoken lines are set in stone.
